title: Views as values, and a body that runs again

videos.script: A view in SwiftUI is not a thing on the screen. It is a small value that describes part of the screen. {{value}} You create it, SwiftUI reads it, and it is thrown away. Next time, a new one. {{some}} Its body returns some View. One type, which the compiler knows and you never write. You will see the compiler refuse a body that tries to return two. {{again}} And the body runs again. Not once, but whenever something it read has changed. {{count}} So you play SwiftUI's part by hand, with the same Observation framework it uses, and count the runs. A change the body never read runs nothing. {{builder}} Then the trick that lets a body list several views. A result builder, which you write yourself in a few lines. {{branch}} And what an if inside a body really is. A branch inside a type. Flip it, and the view in that branch is a different view.
